designDecisions: Decision: R3-F01 is an implementer edit, not an operator decision. ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand selects active expired runs before its per-run transaction, but inside that transaction rechecks only expiry. It does not recheck active status or whether this is still the request current attempt, and abandonment does not release or clear the expired lease. HvRetryDecision then changes the request without a terminal-state guard. Rationale: Contract counterexample, not an execution of proposed code: sweep A and sweep B both select expired run R. A abandons R and queues its request. A new run R2 is claimed and may complete. B enters its transaction for R: the old expiry still has passed, so B abandons R again and applies HvRetryDecision to the now Running or Completed request. It becomes Queued or Failed, possibly releasing turns and emitting a false terminal notification. The artifact-worker sweep at 1747 explicitly rechecks active state and refuses an accepted request; that round 2 repair was not propagated to the HV sweep. SerializableWrite cannot repair a stale candidate unless its delegate revalidates the state. Alternative rejected: approval while the stated counterexample violates an existing requirement. Change required: Make expiry an idempotent, guarded transition in the transaction: re-read active run status, current ownership/attempt and request eligibility, and skip an already settled or superseded candidate. Ensure terminal requests cannot be revived. Cover two sweepers with an intervening claim and an intervening successful finalization, with named tests in FR/TR/TEST-MCP-HVPIPE-007 at H3 and the finalization case at H7; update the policy, unit, caller diagrams and phase bindings.

Decision: R3-F02 is an implementer edit, not an operator decision. RecordRead enlists its ledger row in the caller transaction when one exists. CloseHvRunOutputCommand then consumes and verifies the probe chunks inside that same transaction. The read audit is only committed after the consumption that it is required to precede. Rationale: The AuditLedgerGuard diagram explicitly says read recorded with the caller commit. A crash, transaction conflict or commit failure after ReadinessProbeVerdict consumes bytes rolls back the read row. The evidence was consumed but no durable read record remains. Checking that DataAuditLogs is writable and staging a row are not a durable audit of that access. This contradicts S-29, R-19 and I-13 and leaves the internal-reader part of R2-F08 unresolved. Alternative rejected: approval while the stated counterexample violates an existing requirement. Change required: Specify a durable audit boundary that succeeds before any evidence byte is consumed and survives a subsequent caller rollback. Preserve fencing and probe-state concurrency without claiming an uncommitted row is durable. Add named probe-read rollback/crash/commit-failure cases to the existing audit requirement, with the mock gate first and H3 binding, and propagate the boundary to every internal reader and its caller outcome.

Decision: R3-F03 is an implementer edit, not an operator decision. SubmitHvRequestCommand returns the stored request and its current state on the same-key replay. Its HvRequestResult includes the current run last 20 output lines; only page summaries are exempted. That path has EnsureAvailable but no RecordRead, and is absent from the canonical evidence-reader list. Rationale: Replay an accepted submission after the reviewer has emitted a chunk. The specified same-input path goes directly from IdempotentCreate to 200 HvRequestResult. Returning its lastOutput must read/decompress stored evidence, yet no read row is required and the Submit error list describes evidence_corrupt only for the original admission round trip. A reachable public read therefore bypasses the new audited boundary. Alternative rejected: approval while the stated counterexample violates an existing requirement. Change required: Define one consistent replay projection: either use the canonical audited current-request projection, including corruption and audit-refusal outcomes, or explicitly define a distinct output-free submission response everywhere it is used. Add a named replay-after-output test, ledger-refusal test and corrupt-output case at a phase with stored run output and the relevant surface. Update DTOs, Submit activity/sequence, reader/component user lists, FR/TR/TEST and phase ownership.

Decision: R3-F04 is an implementer edit, not an operator decision. HostileReviewAttemptOutcome contains executionId but no actual model, effort, agent/source, template/version, start/end, or optional token/runtime metadata. CompleteHostileReviewAttemptCommand is nevertheless told to write the execution row with its metadata, without a source or parameter carrying it. Attempt.ExecutionId is written only on the first renewal, so a process that exits before RenewalInterval has no specified writer for that relationship. EndedUtc is set only on success, not on failure or cancellation. Rationale: The host diagram permits reviewer exited before any renewal timer. Complete accepts a Claimed attempt, writes an execution row from Outcome.executionId, and finishes without setting the attempt ExecutionId. The existing execution entity requires ReviewerAgent, Model and Effort and holds SourceSurface, PromptTemplateId, PromptVersion, StartedUtc, EndedUtc and token counts. Those values cannot be reconstructed faithfully from the declared completion DTO, especially actual-versus-configured identity. The stored requirement demands execution metadata and omission with a diagnostic when optional metrics are unavailable. A sentence promising metadata does not define the missing data flow. Alternative rejected: approval while the stated counterexample violates an existing requirement. Change required: Define a canonical normalized execution-metadata contract and its producer, carrying actual identity and the required timing/template fields plus optional metrics or explicit unavailability diagnostics. Define writers for ExecutionId and every terminal timestamp on fast success, failure, cancellation, expiry and no-launch outcomes, preserving the no-raw-artifact rule. Add named fast-exit and metadata/missing-metric cases through TEST-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 in H0 after approval and bind them in H3. Reconcile all units, DTOs and B.9.

Decision: R3-F05 is an implementer edit, not an operator decision. The repaired finalizer describes FailHvRunCommand refusals, but the worker/sweep activities still do not preserve those outcomes. HvWorkerHost continues from Finalize to FileIncident to Claim without branching on audit_unavailable. RunReviewerProcess routes Fail calls directly to Queued/Failed/Canceled or Canceled exits even when Fail refuses. The internal grade unit also declares a non-retryable conflicting existing grade without a corresponding finalizer continuation. Rationale: For a corrupt request brief, FailHvRunCommand may return 503 without changing the Running request. Diagram 1511 to 1512 nevertheless states request Queued Failed or Canceled. The cancel and corrupt-output branches have the same problem. At 1479 any unit 503 must stop the iteration; diagram 1493 to 1494 instead advances through subsequent write-capable units. Generic correct prose at 1502 does not make these unconditional state claims or omitted response branches consistent. This is the worker/sweep propagation specifically required by R2-F09, not the repaired R1-F21 late-Fail overwrite. Alternative rejected: approval while the stated counterexample violates an existing requirement. Change required: Use an explicit common result dispatch or complete branches for every internal call. On audit refusal preserve unchanged state and stop; on stale fence stop without a write; retry conflicts only through the specified guards; advertise Queued/Failed/Canceled only after the failure transition succeeds. Define the grade-conflict continuation. Propagate to host/process/activity/sequence contracts and named refusal/concurrency tests in their H3 or H7 owning phase.

Decision: R3-F06 is an implementer edit, not an operator decision. The error catalog defines evidence_corrupt as public HTTP 500 and immediately lists it among internal codes never returned by a public route. HvOutputEvent names errorCode and closedStatus while the stream wire events use code and status. The GetHvRequest sequence returns 200 after a recorded read without the newly specified decompression-failure response; the Submit sequence likewise omits admission corruption. GzipCodec users still omit the added brief and probe readers. Rationale: A corrupt current-run chunk is required to produce 500 by 599 and the GetHvRequest unit, but the complete request sequence at 1952 to 1953 has only the successful 200 branch after the read is recorded. A client generated from 545 cannot read the stream error field emitted by 576 under the stated DTO shape. These are externally observable contracts, not wording polish. The added corruption cases have not been propagated to every definition and response sequence as R2-F10 required. Alternative rejected: approval while the stated counterexample violates an existing requirement. Change required: Choose one canonical wire shape for each output event and one public/internal error classification, then make DTOs, route responses, sequences, use-case alternates, client contracts and component user lists refer to it consistently. Explicitly draw the admission and last-output corruption responses. Extend the existing named corruption test to assert the exact event field and HTTP status on each affected surface, preserving audited access and server-fault attribution.

Decision: DISAGREE at accuracy 95, completeness 92, confidence 98. Exact store catalog and repaired clauses do not establish functional audit and recovery contracts. Required closure is 13 PASS/5 FAIL; previously passed round 1 items remain credited. D-03 is still the operator approval gate, not a new decision failure.
